title.label: Changed my life! Would recommend one big change though

I LOVE one sec! I've been using it for at least a couple of years now. The combination of using One Sec and deleting the instagram app has basically changed my life. The best features are: 
1. Being able to set time frame blocks for certain apps and websites (so helpful for not scrolling during work hours or late at night!)
2. Being able to set a timer for how many minutes you'd like to spend in the app before another intervention
3. Just making my distracting apps and websites less of a favorable activity (aka more annoying bc I keep getting interrupted!)

I would only make one big change to improve this app. Let's use Facebook for example. When you click on Facebook, it immediately runs OneSec and starts an animation such as the screen going dark for several seconds. This is designed to slow you down and help you consider clearly whether you actually want to be opening that app right now. It's meant to prevent mindlessly opening up apps. When the animation is finished,  it asks you if you really want to open facebook. Well, you've already waited the several seconds for the animation- you may as well open it! You open facebook. 

If onesec asked me if I wanted to open it BEFORE the intervention animation started, that would be a game changer. That way it would be a trade: you have to pay to open this app- you can only open it if you wait several boring seconds first. Then if you click yes to continue to the intervention, and then the intervention finishes, it still asks you what your reason for opening the app is and how many minutes you want to spend on there before another intervention. 

Mane this could be a setting you ca toggle on and off, so if anyone doesn't like that system they can opt out. THEN the app would be perfect. What do we think?

title.label: Strong blocking, but missing real accountability

content.label:
This app does a good job enforcing Screen Time limits, but it falls short as an accountability tool.

Like most Screen Time apps, it relies on three mechanisms:
	•	app time limits
	•	unlocks / temporary access
	•	scheduled blocks

The problem is that following or breaking these rules isn’t meaningfully tracked. Users can:
	•	repeatedly use unlocks
	•	change limits or schedules after enforcement starts
	•	revoke Screen Time permissions and re-enable later

…without any persistent history or consequence inside the app. That makes it easy to undermine your own rules quietly, which defeats the purpose for serious users.

What would make this a 5-star app:
	•	an accountability history (unlock usage, schedule adherence, rule changes)
	•	logging Screen Time permission revocations/restores
	•	an integrity metric (did I keep my word or not)
	•	brief, optional reflection prompts at key moments (before unlocks, after rule changes)
	•	weekly summaries focused on accountability, not just usage minutes
	•	a place to define and revisit why you’re limiting apps, so behavior change is internal, not just enforced

Blocking alone changes behavior temporarily.
Accountability, integrity tracking, and reflection change it long-term.

If these additions were made, this would easily be a 5-star app.
